Rachel / Marissa — quick explainer for the thread so we can reply to Samantha:

- How credits apply: promotional credits in the PLG flow are applied against the net usage charges (token usage) on the billing account. They reduce the amount due for usage.
- VAT / Sales tax handling: tax regulations in the EU require us to calculate VAT on the gross taxable base and remit tax accordingly. In our billing system the tax line can still appear on the invoice even if credits offset the net usage. Essentially the invoice records the gross usage, VAT, and then shows credits/adjustments that reduce the net payable. That can make it look like VAT was charged even when the net due is zero or small.

Example (BR-000345):
  - Gross usage: €78.20
  - VAT (20% theoretical example): €15.64
  - Promotional credit applied: -€93.84
  - Net due: €0.00 (no payment taken)

If the invoice shows a small payment was taken, it means credits were already exhausted at the time of that billing cycle OR the tax collector required a minimal rounding/processing amount. We should verify the transaction log and card/ACH history for the account.

Options we can offer now:
1) If Blackridge is VAT-registered and supplies a valid VAT number, we can issue a VAT-only credit note (refund of the tax portion) if policy allows — finance will need the VAT registration and confirmation.
2) If credits were exhausted and a small token charge was billed, we can reverse that charge and re-apply a discretionary trial top-up while procurement completes.
3) Provide a one-time trial extension and additional self-serve credits tied to your HubSpot deal (HB-4821) to cover any gap; this requires a short authorization from an account owner.

I've attached the invoice stub and the trial-credit terms for reference. Rachel / Marissa, let me know which option Blackridge prefers and we can process via the billing portal.
